newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Polyta says profit falls on rising costs.
newsitem.headline: Polyta says profit falls on rising costs.

text.p: Indonesian petrochemical giant PT Tri Polyta Indonesia said sales in the third quarter of 1996 soared, but net income plunged mainly due to rising raw material costs.

"The third quarter marked continued pressure on our Delta P margin from both sides -- firm pricing for the raw material and weak pricing for the finished products," chief executive officer Markus Hartanto said in a statement.
Delta P is the difference in prices between the finished product polypropylene and propylene, the main raw material.
"However, our strategy to continue a sales volume push, both domestic and export, maintained our profitability," Hartanto said.
Hartanto said net sales for the third quarter of 1996 were 194.5 billion rupiah, up 42.1 percent from net sales of 136.9 billion rupiah in the same period of last year.
Net income, calculated on U.S. accounting principles, plunged to 4.1 billion rupiah in the third quarter of this year against 16.2 billion rupiah during the same period last year.
"Tri Polyta's average Delta P was $285 (per ton) in the third quarter of 1996 compared to the average spread of $549 in the same quarter a year ago," the statement said.
Delta P in the third quarter of 1996 was weak because it reflected higher feedstock prices and soft polypropylene prices, it said.

Unplanned cracker outages and rising demand for propylene derivatives in Europe and the United States had driven up propylene prices while polypropylene prices were weak due to soft Chinese demand, it said.
It said domestic sales volume rose 22.4 percent to 66,540 million tons in the third quarter of this year against 54,361 million tons in the same period of last year.
Export sales also continued to rise to a total of 32,736 million tons in the third quarter of this year, it said without giving comparative figures.
Tri Polyta said it had formed a joint venture distribution company, Trimega Citra Mandiri, with Bukitmega Masabadi, which is Indonesia's largest polypropylene distributor, to boost sales.
Polypropylene resins are petrochemical plastics used to manufacture a wide range of consumer products such as carpet, rope, clothing and automotive parts.
